- Model tends to overestimate prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes.
- Forecasts often peak too early or too high following sharp price increases.
- Model underestimates true price volatility in the first 5–10 days after a spike, then gradually converges.
- Mean reversion is not captured well — model holds high forecasts longer than actual price corrections.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent bias toward higher values, especially when recent history includes high prices.
- Model reacts too slowly to downward trends; underestimates price drops unless preceded by strong prior decline.
- Overshoot correction needed after spikes — reduce forecast by 5–10% in subsequent periods.
- Avoid overfitting to recent high prices — use 10–15 day moving average as a sanity check for forecast anchoring.
